category: Automation III: LiveLink for MATLAB command reference, other LiveLinks, materials & file formats
description: The mph* command set of LiveLink for MATLAB beyond the functions in the first automation chunk (session and file commands, geometry/mesh plotting and statistics, evaluation and integration helpers, matrix and state-space extraction, selection helpers, navigation and inspection, reporting), LiveLink for Simulink and LiveLink for Excel, the material node types (Material Library, Material Link, Switch, Layered Material, External Material, property groups and temperature-dependent material functions, the specialised material libraries) and the import/export file formats (NASTRAN/mesh formats, STL/PLY/3MF, VTK, DXF/CAD, sectionwise and spreadsheet text, Touchstone, Physics Builder archives, images and animations).

tools.name: mphopen / mphsave / mphlaunch / mphcd
tools.description: Session and file helpers of LiveLink for MATLAB: mphopen opens a GUI listing recent model files and returns the chosen model (mphload is the non-interactive loader), mphsave(model, 'file.mph') saves the model (also as .m, .java or .vba by extension; without a file name it saves to the original path), mphlaunch(model) starts a COMSOL Desktop client connected to the MATLAB session's server and opens the model in it so you can inspect it interactively, and mphcd(model) changes MATLAB's current directory to the model's directory. mphthumbnail sets or gets the model thumbnail image.
tools.usage: model = mphopen; mphsave(model, 'C:/out/model_solved.mph'); mphsave(model, 'model.m'); mphlaunch(model); mphcd(model)

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: COMSOL model object from mphload/mphopen/ModelUtil.create.

parameters.name: filename (mphsave)
parameters.description: Target file; extension .mph, .m, .java or .vba selects the format.

parameters.name: mphlaunch options
parameters.description: 'mphlaunch mphserver' variant when no model is given.

tools.notes: mphsave with a .m extension produces the same code as File > Save As Model File for MATLAB. mphlaunch requires a COMSOL Desktop installation on the same machine as MATLAB.

tools.name: mphversion / mphdoc / mphapplicationlibraries / mphshowerrors
tools.description: Information commands: mphversion(model) returns the COMSOL version of the server (and the version that saved the model), mphdoc opens the COMSOL documentation window for a topic or a model node (mphdoc(model, 'ht') opens the Heat Transfer interface documentation), mphapplicationlibraries opens the Application Libraries browser from MATLAB, and mphshowerrors(model) prints the error and warning nodes present in the model tree (the same messages shown as red/yellow markers in the Model Builder), which is the first thing to run when a study fails from a script.
tools.usage: v = mphversion(model); mphdoc(model, 'physics', 'ht'); mphapplicationlibraries; mphshowerrors(model)

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model object.

parameters.name: topic / node tag (mphdoc)
parameters.description: Documentation topic or node to look up.

tools.notes: Java exceptions in MATLAB carry the COMSOL message in ME.message; mphshowerrors adds the node-level details (undefined variables, missing materials).

tools.name: mphgeom
tools.description: Plots a geometry sequence (or a specific geometry feature/object) in a MATLAB figure, with options to show entity numbers (vertex, edge, face, domain labels), to plot only selected entities, to control transparency and colours, and to add the plot to the current axes. Used to check scripted geometries and to identify entity numbers for selections without opening the Desktop.
tools.usage: mphgeom(model, 'geom1'); mphgeom(model, 'geom1', 'facelabels', 'on', 'facealpha', 0.5); mphgeom(model, 'geom1', 'edgelabels', 'on'); mphgeom(model, 'geom1', 'feature', 'blk1')

parameters.name: geomtag
parameters.description: Geometry sequence tag.

parameters.name: 'facelabels' / 'edgelabels' / 'vertexlabels' / 'domainlabels'
parameters.description: Show entity numbers ('on'/'off').

parameters.name: 'feature' / 'entity' / 'selection'
parameters.description: Plot a feature's output, a given entity level, or a named selection.

parameters.name: 'facealpha' / 'facecolor' / 'edgecolor' / 'parent' / 'view'
parameters.description: Appearance and target axes.

tools.notes: The geometry must be built (model.geom('geom1').run) first. mphviewselection plots a named selection highlighted in the geometry.

tools.name: mphmesh / mphmeshstats
tools.description: mphmesh(model, 'mesh1') plots a mesh in a MATLAB figure (with 'edgemode', 'facemode', 'meshcolor', 'edgecolor', 'vertexmode', 'parent' and 'edgelabels'/'facelabels' options), and mphmeshstats(model, 'mesh1') returns a structure with mesh statistics - number of elements per type, quality measures (min/mean), element size range, number of vertices - and optionally the mesh data itself ([stats, data] = mphmeshstats(...)) with vertex coordinates, element connectivity and entity indices for use in custom MATLAB postprocessing or export.
tools.usage: mphmesh(model, 'mesh1'); stats = mphmeshstats(model, 'mesh1'); [stats, data] = mphmeshstats(model, 'mesh1')

parameters.name: meshtag
parameters.description: Mesh sequence tag.

parameters.name: 'edgemode' / 'facemode' / 'meshcolor'
parameters.description: Plot options (mphmesh).

parameters.name: stats fields
parameters.description: numelem, minquality, meanquality, qualitymeasure, hasproblems, etc.

parameters.name: data fields
parameters.description: vertex (coordinates), elem (connectivity per type), elementity (entity index per element), types.

tools.notes: Element indices in data are 0-based (Java convention); add 1 for MATLAB. mphxmeshinfo gives the extended mesh (DOF-level) information instead.

tools.name: mphplot
tools.description: Renders a plot group of the model in a MATLAB figure (mphplot(model, 'pg1')) using COMSOL's plot data, or plots the data structure returned by mpheval/mphinterp/mphsurf directly; options select the solution number/parameter ('rangenum'), the plot index within the group ('index'), the color table, whether to show the color bar, and 'server','on' to have the COMSOL server render the picture instead of MATLAB graphics. It is the quickest way to get a COMSOL-quality plot into a MATLAB figure for further annotation or subplot layouts.
tools.usage: mphplot(model, 'pg1'); mphplot(model, 'pg1', 'rangenum', 3); mphplot(model, 'pg2', 'index', 1); pd = mpheval(model, 'T', 'edim', 3); mphplot(pd, 1)

parameters.name: pgtag
parameters.description: Plot group tag (pg1, pg2 ...).

parameters.name: 'rangenum'
parameters.description: Solution index (time step/parameter) to plot for multi-solution datasets.

parameters.name: 'index'
parameters.description: Plot feature index inside the group.

parameters.name: 'colortable' / 'colorbar' / 'server' / 'parent'
parameters.description: Appearance and rendering target.

tools.notes: Some plot types (e.g. streamlines, arrows on unstructured data) render only with 'server','on'. mphimage exports the server-rendered image directly to a file.

tools.name: mphmax / mphmin / mphmean
tools.description: Convenience evaluators returning the maximum, minimum or mean of an expression over the geometry (or a selection at a given entity level) for each solution in a dataset: mphmax(model, 'T', 'volume') gives the volume maximum of T, with options 'selection', 'dataset', 'solnum', 'unit', 'edim' and 'outersolnum'; mphmean integrates and divides by the measure. They wrap the Derived Values Maximum/Minimum/Average nodes without creating them in the model.
tools.usage: Tmax = mphmax(model, 'T', 'volume'); Tmin = mphmin(model, 'T', 'surface', 'selection', [3 4]); Tmean = mphmean(model, 'T', 'volume', 'dataset', 'dset1', 'solnum', 'end')

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression or cell array of expressions.

parameters.name: 'volume' | 'surface' | 'line' | 'point'
parameters.description: Entity level for the evaluation.

parameters.name: 'selection' / 'dataset' / 'solnum' / 'outersolnum'
parameters.description: Entities and solutions to evaluate.

parameters.name: 'unit'
parameters.description: Output unit.

tools.notes: Maximum/minimum are evaluated on element nodes/Gauss points, so slight differences to plots are normal. mphint2 (first chunk) is the integration counterpart.

tools.name: mphevalpoint / mphevalpointmatrix / mphevalglobalmatrix
tools.description: Point-based evaluations: mphevalpoint(model, 'T', 'selection', 5) evaluates expressions at geometry vertices (points) for all solutions, mphevalpointmatrix evaluates matrix-valued point quantities (e.g. impedance matrices defined at points), and mphevalglobalmatrix(model, 'emw.S') returns global matrix variables such as S-parameter, capacitance or inductance matrices as MATLAB matrices (per solution/frequency) - the scripted form of Global Matrix Evaluation.
tools.usage: Tp = mphevalpoint(model, 'T', 'selection', [2 5]); S = mphevalglobalmatrix(model, 'emw.S'); Sdb = mphevalglobalmatrix(model, 'emw.S', 'dataset', 'dset1', 'solnum', 1:20)

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Point expression or matrix variable name.

parameters.name: 'selection'
parameters.description: Point entity numbers (mphevalpoint).

parameters.name: 'dataset' / 'solnum' / 'outersolnum' / 'unit'
parameters.description: Solution and unit selection.

tools.notes: Point evaluations use the geometry vertex, not arbitrary coordinates; use mphinterp for arbitrary points.

tools.name: mphtable / mphgetu / mphsolinfo / mphsolutioninfo
tools.description: Result-data accessors: mphtable(model, 'tbl1') returns a results table (probe tables, derived values) as a structure with data, headers and units; mphgetu(model) returns the raw solution vector(s) (DOF values, optionally derivatives 'type','ut' and a chosen solution number) for custom processing or as initial values; mphsolinfo(model) reports which solver sequences exist, their sizes, parameter names and values, time steps and the dataset they belong to; mphsolutioninfo(model, 'parameters', {'L', 0.1}) finds the solution numbers and datasets matching given parameter values.
tools.usage: t = mphtable(model, 'tbl1'); U = mphgetu(model, 'soltag', 'sol1', 'solnum', 'end'); info = mphsolinfo(model, 'soltag', 'sol1'); si = mphsolutioninfo(model, 'parameters', {'freq', 1e9})

parameters.name: tbltag
parameters.description: Table tag.

parameters.name: 'soltag' / 'solnum' / 'type'
parameters.description: Solver sequence, solution number(s), and 'sol'|'ut'|'utt' for derivatives (mphgetu).

parameters.name: 'parameters'
parameters.description: Name/value cell pairs to match (mphsolutioninfo).

tools.notes: DOF ordering from mphgetu is explained by mphxmeshinfo (which DOF belongs to which variable and node).

tools.name: mphmodel / mphtags / mphgetexpressions / mphgetproperties
tools.description: Model inspection: mphmodel(model) lists the tags of the top-level nodes (and mphmodel(model.physics('ht')) the children of any node), mphtags(node) returns the tags and display names of the children of a node, mphgetexpressions(model.param) or (model.variable('var1')) returns the names, expressions and descriptions of parameters/variables as a cell array, and mphgetproperties(node) returns all properties of a feature as a MATLAB structure (property names and values) - the MATLAB equivalent of properties()/getString() used to discover settings before scripting them.
tools.usage: mphmodel(model); mphmodel(model.component('comp1').physics('ht')); [tags, names] = mphtags(model.study); p = mphgetexpressions(model.param); s = mphgetproperties(model.component('comp1').physics('ht').feature('hf1'))

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: Any model node object (model, model.param, physics feature, ...).

parameters.name: mphmodel option '-struct'
parameters.description: Return the tree as a nested structure.

tools.notes: mphnavigator (first chunk) is the graphical version of these functions. Property values are returned in COMSOL's string form (with units) where applicable.

tools.name: mphgetselection / mphselectbox / mphselectcoords / mphviewselection
tools.description: Selection helpers: mphgetselection(model.selection('box1')) returns the entities of a selection node (entity numbers, dimension, geometry), mphselectbox(model, 'geom1', [xmin xmax; ymin ymax; zmin zmax], 'boundary') returns the entities inside a box (rubber-band selection by coordinates, with 'include','any'|'all' for partial inclusion), mphselectcoords(model, 'geom1', [x y z]', 'point', 'radius', 1e-6) returns entities at or near given coordinates (the scripted way to find the boundary number of a face at a known location, robust to renumbering), and mphviewselection plots a selection highlighted on the geometry.
tools.usage: sel = mphgetselection(model.component('comp1').selection('box1')); idx = mphselectbox(model, 'geom1', [0 0.1; 0 0.05; 0 0.02], 'boundary'); idx = mphselectcoords(model, 'geom1', [0.05; 0.025; 0.02], 'boundary', 'radius', 1e-3); mphviewselection(model, 'geom1', idx, 'boundary')

parameters.name: geomtag
parameters.description: Geometry tag.

parameters.name: box / coords
parameters.description: Coordinate limits (dim x 2) or point coordinates (dim x N).

parameters.name: 'domain' | 'boundary' | 'edge' | 'point'
parameters.description: Entity level returned.

parameters.name: 'include' / 'radius'
parameters.description: Partial-inclusion rule for boxes; search radius for coordinates.

tools.notes: Coordinates are in the geometry length unit. Using these instead of hard-coded entity numbers keeps scripts valid when the geometry changes.

tools.name: mphmatrix / mphinputmatrix
tools.description: System-matrix extraction: mphmatrix(model, 'sol1', 'out', {'K', 'L', 'M', 'N', 'D', 'E', 'Kc', 'Lc', 'Dc', 'Ec', 'Null', 'Nullf', 'ud', 'uscale'}) assembles and returns the stiffness matrix K, load vector L, constraint matrices N/M, damping/mass matrices D/E, and their eliminated (constraint-free) versions Kc, Lc, Dc, Ec as MATLAB sparse matrices from a solver sequence (Compile Equations + Dependent Variables nodes must exist), enabling custom solvers, model order reduction and eigenanalysis in MATLAB; mphinputmatrix(model, 'sol1', 'sol1', 'K', K, ...) feeds modified matrices back into a solver so COMSOL solves a system altered in MATLAB.
tools.usage: M = mphmatrix(model, 'sol1', 'out', {'Kc', 'Lc'}, 'initmethod', 'init'); u = M.Kc \ M.Lc; mphinputmatrix(model, 'sol1', 'sol1', 'K', Knew, 'L', Lnew)

parameters.name: soltag
parameters.description: Solver sequence (with StudyStep and Variables nodes).

parameters.name: 'out'
parameters.description: Cell array of matrix names to return.

parameters.name: 'initmethod' / 'initsol' / 'solnum'
parameters.description: Linearisation point: initial values or an existing solution.

parameters.name: 'extractsensitivity' / 'sparse'
parameters.description: Additional options.

tools.notes: Matrices are assembled at the current linearisation point; nonlinear problems give the tangent matrices. Eliminated matrices (Kc) are what a Newton step uses; the scaling must be undone as shown to obtain physical values.

tools.name: mphstate / mphreduction
tools.description: State-space extraction: mphstate(model, 'sol1', 'out', {'A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'Mc', 'Null', 'ud', 'x0'}, 'input', {'V_in'}, 'output', {'T_probe'}) linearises the model around a solution and returns the state-space matrices (dx/dt = A x + B u, y = C x + D u) for chosen input parameters and output expressions, for use with the MATLAB Control System Toolbox or Simulink; mphreduction(model, 'sol1', ...) does the same for a reduced-order model built with the Model Reduction study (modal or Krylov basis), returning small matrices suitable for real-time simulation.
tools.usage: S = mphstate(model, 'sol1', 'out', {'A', 'B', 'C', 'D'}, 'input', {'Vin'}, 'output', {'T_out'}); sys = ss(full(S.A), full(S.B), full(S.C), full(S.D)); R = mphreduction(model, 'sol2', 'out', {'Ar', 'Br', 'Cr', 'Dr'})

parameters.name: 'input'
parameters.description: Global parameters acting as inputs (must appear in the model's loads/sources).

parameters.name: 'output'
parameters.description: Global expressions (probes, operators) taken as outputs.

parameters.name: 'out'
parameters.description: Matrices to return (A, B, C, D, Mc, Null, ud, x0, ...).

parameters.name: 'sparse'
parameters.description: Return sparse matrices.

tools.notes: The model must be linear (or linearised) with the inputs entering linearly; the Model Reduction study in COMSOL (see the studies chunk) exports the same reduced matrices from the GUI. LiveLink for Simulink builds a Simulink block from these matrices or co-simulates the full model.

tools.name: mphxmeshinfo
tools.description: Returns the extended mesh information of a solver sequence - the mapping between DOFs and mesh nodes/elements: fields such as ndofs, fieldnames, fieldndofs, dofs (dofnames, coords, nodes), nodes (coords, dofs), elements per type (with DOF indices) and the geometry entity of each element - needed to interpret solution vectors from mphgetu and matrices from mphmatrix, to build custom fields, or to implement your own solver loop with COMSOL assembly.
tools.usage: info = mphxmeshinfo(model); info = mphxmeshinfo(model, 'soltag', 'sol1', 'studysteptag', 'st1'); coords = info.dofs.coords; names = info.dofs.dofnames

parameters.name: 'soltag' / 'studysteptag'
parameters.description: Solver sequence and StudyStep node to describe (default the first).

parameters.name: 'meshtag'
parameters.description: Mesh to describe when no solver exists.

tools.notes: Indices are 0-based in the returned structure (Java); nameinds + 1 maps to MATLAB indexing. Higher-order elements have DOFs at mid-side points that are not mesh vertices.

tools.name: mphmeasure / mphgetcoords / mphgetadj
tools.description: Geometry queries: mphmeasure(model, 'geom1', 'domain', 'selection', 2) returns volume/area/length, centre of mass and bounding box of selected entities (the scripted Measure tool), mphgetcoords(model, 'geom1', 'point', [1 2 3]) returns the coordinates of geometry vertices (or the coordinates describing edges/boundaries), and mphgetadj(model, 'geom1', 'boundary', 'domain', 2) returns the entities adjacent to given entities (e.g. all boundaries of domain 2, or the domains adjacent to a boundary) so selections can be derived topologically in scripts.
tools.usage: m = mphmeasure(model, 'geom1', 'domain', 'selection', 1); V = m.volume; c = mphgetcoords(model, 'geom1', 'point', 3); bnd = mphgetadj(model, 'geom1', 'boundary', 'domain', 2)

parameters.name: geomtag
parameters.description: Built geometry.

parameters.name: entity level / 'selection'
parameters.description: 'domain'|'boundary'|'edge'|'point' and entity numbers.

parameters.name: mphgetadj(model, geom, returnlevel, inputlevel, entities)
parameters.description: Adjacency query direction.

tools.notes: mphgetadj works on the finalized geometry; the equivalent Definitions node is the Adjacent selection.

tools.name: mphinterpolationfile / mphreadstl / mphwritestl / mphimage2geom
tools.description: Data-file helpers: mphinterpolationfile(data, header, filename) writes MATLAB arrays in the sectionwise/spreadsheet text format that the Interpolation function reads, so measured or computed fields become COMSOL functions; mphreadstl(filename) reads an STL file into a structure of vertices/faces (for inspection or repair in MATLAB) and mphwritestl(filename, plotdata) writes plot data (from mpheval/mphsurf, e.g. a deformed surface) as STL for 3D printing or CAD; mphimage2geom(imagedata, level) converts an image matrix into a 2D geometry object (contours at a grey level become curves/solids), the programmatic Image to Curve.
tools.usage: mphinterpolationfile(data, 'x y T', 'field.txt'); s = mphreadstl('part.stl'); mphwritestl('surface.stl', pd); model = mphimage2geom(imread('mask.png'), 128, 'type', 'solid')

parameters.name: data / header
parameters.description: N x (nargs + nvalues) matrix and column header for interpolation files.

parameters.name: plotdata
parameters.description: Structure from mpheval/mphsurf with vertices and triangles (mphwritestl).

parameters.name: level / 'type' / 'scale'
parameters.description: Grey-level threshold, geometry type (curve|solid) and scaling for image conversion.

tools.notes: For large grids use the spreadsheet format with the grid option in the Interpolation function for faster evaluation.

tools.name: mphparticle / mphray / mphevaluate / mphreport / mphimage
tools.description: Remaining helpers: mphparticle(model, 'dataset', 'part1', 'expr', {'qx', 'qy', 'cpt.V'}) and mphray evaluate expressions along particle/ray trajectories (per particle and time) as MATLAB arrays; mphevaluate(model, 'L', 'm') evaluates a parameter expression with unit conversion (the scripted model.param.evaluate); mphreport(model, 'rpt1') generates a report defined in the model (or creates one with 'type','brief'|'intermediate'|'complete' and a file name); mphimage(model, 'pg1', 'file.png') renders a plot group on the server and writes the image file (alternative to mphplot + print).
tools.usage: pd = mphparticle(model, 'dataset', 'part1', 'expr', {'qx','qy','qz'}); L = mphevaluate(model, 'L', 'mm'); mphreport(model, 'rpt1'); mphreport(model, 'type', 'brief', 'filename', 'report.html'); mphimage(model, 'pg1', 'T.png', 'width', 1200)

parameters.name: 'dataset' / 'expr' / 'solnum' (mphparticle, mphray)
parameters.description: Particle/ray dataset, expressions and time steps.

parameters.name: expr / unit (mphevaluate)
parameters.description: Parameter expression and desired unit.

parameters.name: rpttag or 'type' / 'filename' (mphreport)
parameters.description: Existing report node or a new report of a given level.

parameters.name: pgtag / filename / 'width' / 'height' (mphimage)
parameters.description: Plot group and image output settings.

tools.notes: mphimage requires the server started with graphics support (comsol mphserver -graphics or the default on Windows). mphaddplotdata adds MATLAB data as a plot to the model.

tools.name: LiveLink for Simulink
tools.description: Couples a COMSOL model with Simulink by cosimulation: in COMSOL 6.4 you add a Cosimulation export node that writes an FMU/cosimulation file with the chosen inputs and outputs, and in Simulink you place the COMSOL Cosimulation block from the LiveLink library and point it at that file. Simulink then drives the COMSOL solver at every communication step.
tools.usage: COMSOL: add a Cosimulation export (inputs = global parameters, outputs = global expressions) and compile it; Simulink: LiveLink for Simulink library > COMSOL Cosimulation block > select the exported file; MATLAB helpers mphsimsettings / mphupdatesystem.

parameters.name: Model file / study
parameters.description: .mph and the time-dependent study used for cosimulation.

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Global parameters set from Simulink signals each step.

parameters.name: Outputs
parameters.description: Global expressions/probes returned to Simulink.

parameters.name: Fixed step / solver settings
parameters.description: COMSOL solves from t to t+dt for each Simulink step.

tools.notes: Cosimulation is slow (a COMSOL solve per Simulink step); use reduced-order state space where linearity allows. Documentation: LiveLink for Simulink User's Guide. Replaces the older state-space export workflow; FMU cosimulation is the documented route in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: LiveLink for Excel
tools.description: Add-in that adds a COMSOL tab to Microsoft Excel for opening a model, showing its parameters and variables in worksheet cells (editable, with units), running studies, and importing results (derived values, tables, plots as images) into the workbook, so engineers can drive parameter studies from spreadsheets; it also enables Excel files as material-property and interpolation-data sources (File > Import from Excel in Interpolation functions and Materials), VBA model files (.vba) recorded from the COMSOL Desktop, and running apps from Excel.
tools.usage: Excel ribbon > COMSOL tab > Open model > Parameters (write to cells) > Compute > Results > Table/Plot; Save As > Model File for VBA in COMSOL Desktop for VBA automation

parameters.name: Parameters / Variables sheets
parameters.description: Cells linked to model parameters; changes are sent to COMSOL.

parameters.name: Compute
parameters.description: Runs the selected study on the connected COMSOL server.

parameters.name: Results import
parameters.description: Tables and images inserted into the workbook.

parameters.name: VBA API
parameters.description: The full COMSOL API accessible from VBA through the .vba model file syntax.

tools.example:
' VBA (from a saved Model File for VBA)
Dim model As Object
Set model = ModelUtil.Create("Model")
model.param.set "L", "0.1[m]"
model.study("std1").run
model.save "C:\out\model.mph"
tools.notes: Requires LiveLink for Excel licence and Excel for Windows; the COMSOL server is started by the add-in. Interpolation functions can read .xlsx sheets directly when the add-in is installed.

tools.name: Material Library (product) and built-in material databases
tools.description: Materials come from databases in the Add Material window: the Built-In database of COMSOL Multiphysics (air, water, common metals, silicon, glasses with basic properties), module-specific libraries (AC/DC: nonlinear magnetic B-H curves and Jiles-Atherton parameters; RF/Wave Optics/Ray Optics: Optical materials with n(lambda) dispersion; Piezoelectric materials; MEMS materials; Semiconductor materials; Bioheat tissue; Battery, Fuel Cell, Corrosion, Electrodeposition electrolytes and electrodes; Liquids and Gases with temperature-dependent properties; Thermodynamics property packages) and the optional Material Library product with over 12 000 materials and temperature-dependent property functions (metals, alloys, polymers, ceramics, minerals) with references. Materials are added to a component with their properties as functions of temperature where available.
tools.usage: Materials > Add Material (or Home > Add Material) > Built-In / Material Library / module libraries > search > Add to Component; API: model.component("comp1").material().create(...) plus the property definitions the GUI generates

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Full-text search over material names and properties.

parameters.name: Add to Component / Add to Global Materials
parameters.description: Where the material node is created.

parameters.name: Property functions
parameters.description: Temperature-dependent properties as Piecewise/Analytic/Interpolation functions with validity ranges (Material Library).

parameters.name: User-Defined Library
parameters.description: Save your own materials for reuse (Materials > Add to User-Defined Library).

tools.example:
rem GUI: Add Material > Material Library > Stainless steel 304 (annealed) > Add to Component
rem then in physics: Heat Transfer > Solid uses k(T), Cp(T), rho(T) from the material automatically
rem Java (recorded): model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup("def").func().create("k", "Piecewise"); ... set("thermalconductivity", new String[]{"k(T[1/K])[W/(m*K)]"})
tools.notes: The Material Library product is a separate licence; module libraries come with their modules. Missing properties show as warnings in the physics settings ('Material property ... is missing'); add them in the material's Basic property group.

tools.name: Material Link / Material Switch
tools.description: Material node types for reuse and variants: a Material Link (Materials > More Materials > Material Link, or under Global Definitions > Materials) assigns a global material to a selection in a component so the same definition is shared by several components or selections; a Material Switch (Switch) holds several materials as children and a switch index selects the active one, driven by a Material Sweep study step to compare materials in one run. Both behave like ordinary materials in the physics settings.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Materials > (add material); Component > Materials > Material Link (matlnk1) > Link to material; Component > Materials > Switch (matsw1) with child materials; API: model.material().create("mat1", "Common") (global); model.component("comp1").material().create("matlnk1", "Link"); matlnk1.set("link", "mat1"); model.component("comp1").material().create("matsw1", "Switch")

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: Tag of the global material referenced by a Material Link.

parameters.name: Switch children
parameters.description: Materials inside the Switch node; the active one is chosen by the switch index / Material Sweep.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: Entities the link or switch applies to.

tools.notes: Global materials cannot be assigned directly - always through a link. Material Switch requires all children to define the properties the physics needs.

tools.name: Layered Material / Layered Material Link / Layered Material Stack
tools.description: Global Definitions material nodes describing laminates: a Layered Material lists layers (name, material link, rotation angle, thickness, mesh elements through the thickness) that define a lay-up; Layered Material Link assigns a lay-up to boundaries in a component and Layered Material Stack combines several lay-ups (with interface materials) into one; the Layer Stack Preview and Layer Cross Section Preview plot the definition. Used by Layered Shell, Shell (layered linear elastic), Heat Transfer in Shells, Electric Currents in Shells, Piezoelectricity Layered Shell and the Composite Materials Module failure criteria; results use the Layered Material dataset and Layered Material Slice / Through Thickness plots.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Materials > Layered Material (lmat1): layer table; Component > Materials > Layered Material Link (llmat1) > Layered material: lmat1, selection: boundaries; API: model.material().create("lmat1", "LayeredMaterial"); lmat1.set("layername", ...); set("link", ...); set("rotation", ...); set("thickness", ...); model.component("comp1").material().create("llmat1", "LayeredMaterialLink"); llmat1.set("link", "lmat1")

parameters.name: layername / link / rotation / thickness / meshPoints
parameters.description: Per-layer definition arrays.

parameters.name: Interface materials (Stack)
parameters.description: Thin interface layers between lay-ups.

parameters.name: Position / offset
parameters.description: Where the reference surface lies in the thickness (midplane, top, bottom, user).

tools.notes: Available in the core product for thin-layer thermal/electrical features; layered structural analysis with ply failure needs the Composite Materials Module. The 'Layered Shell (lshell)' entry describes the structural interface.

tools.name: External Material (user-defined material models in C)
tools.description: Global Definitions > Materials > External Material lets a compiled shared library (C/C++, following the COMSOL external-material interface) supply a complete constitutive model: for Solid Mechanics a General stress-strain relation, Inelastic residual strain or Inelastic residual deformation model receiving strains/state variables and returning stresses and tangent matrices, and for Magnetic Fields a General H-B relation; the material is then selected in the physics (External Stress-Strain Relation / External Magnetic Material nodes). It is the path for proprietary or research constitutive laws that the built-in models cannot express.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Materials > External Material (extmat1): Interface type (General stress-strain relation | Inelastic residual strain | ... | General H-B relation), Library path, state variables; Physics > Solid Mechanics > Material Models > External Stress-Strain Relation; API: model.material().create("extmat1", "External"); extmat1.set("path", "C:/lib/mymodel.dll")

parameters.name: Interface type
parameters.description: Which callback signature the library implements.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Shared library (DLL/.so/.dylib).

parameters.name: Model inputs / parameters / state variables
parameters.description: Values passed to the library and internal state stored per integration point.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics/Nonlinear Structural Materials (or AC/DC for H-B) Module; example C sources and the header are in the COMSOL installation (doc/external_material). The library must be compiled for the platform running the solver (also on cluster nodes).

tools.name: Material property groups and temperature-dependent property functions
tools.description: Each material node holds property groups: Basic (def) with density, heat capacity, conductivities, permittivity etc., plus groups added when a physics needs them (Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio (Enu), Lame parameters, Thermal Expansion, Refractive index, Piezoelectric strain/stress-charge coupling, B-H curve, Hyperelastic model constants...). Any property can be an expression of the Model Inputs (T, p, c, strain...) - typically via functions defined inside the group (Piecewise polynomials with validity ranges as in the Material Library, Interpolation from measured tables, Analytic formulas) referenced like k(T[1/K])[W/(m*K)] - and the Material Contents section of the settings window shows which properties are required by the physics, missing, or defined.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Material Contents table (edit values/expressions); mat1 > Basic > Functions (right-click: Add Function); Property group: right-click mat1 > Add property group; API: mat1.propertyGroup("def").func().create("k_T", "Interpolation"); mat1.propertyGroup("def").set("thermalconductivity", new String[]{"k_T(T[1/K])[W/(m*K)]"}); mat1.propertyGroup("def").addInput("temperature")

parameters.name: propertyGroup(name)
parameters.description: def | Enu | Lame | ThermalExpansion | RefractiveIndex | BHCurve | PiezoelectricStrainCharge | ... (created by physics or manually).

parameters.name: func().create(tag, type)
parameters.description: Functions local to the group (Interpolation, Piecewise, Analytic).

parameters.name: addInput("temperature"|"pressure"|"concentration"|...)
parameters.description: Declares the model inputs the properties depend on so the physics passes its variables.

parameters.name: Anisotropic properties
parameters.description: Given as 3x3 tensor components (9 strings) with 'Anisotropic' or 'Diagonal' type.

tools.notes: Function arguments must be dimensionless inside the material (hence T[1/K]) and the result given a unit. The physics' Model Inputs section decides which temperature variable is passed (Common model input, a heat interface's T, or a user value).

tools.name: Optical / Piezoelectric / Nonlinear Magnetic / MEMS / Semiconductor material libraries
tools.description: Module-specific material databases in the Add Material window: the Optical library (Wave Optics, Ray Optics, RF) provides refractive index and extinction coefficient versus wavelength for glasses (Schott, Ohara, CDGM...), crystals, polymers, metals (Johnson-Christy, Rakic) as interpolation/Sellmeier functions; the Piezoelectric library (Structural, MEMS, Acoustics) gives full elasticity, coupling and permittivity matrices for PZT-4/5A/5H/8, barium titanate, quartz, lithium niobate/tantalate, AlN, ZnO, PVDF; the Nonlinear Magnetic library (AC/DC) provides B-H curves and Jiles-Atherton hysteresis data for electrical steels, soft ferrites, permalloy, and permanent magnet materials with remanence and coercivity; the MEMS library has silicon (anisotropic), polysilicon, SiO2, SiN, metals with piezoresistive coefficients; the Semiconductor library carries band structure, mobility and recombination data for Si, Ge, GaAs, InP, GaN and other compounds.
tools.usage: Add Material > (module) Optical / Piezoelectric / Nonlinear Magnetic / MEMS / Semiconductor > material > Add to Component; the physics picks the required property group automatically (e.g. Refractive index, Piezoelectric strain-charge, B-H curve)

parameters.name: Optical: n(lambda), k(lambda)
parameters.description: Dispersion functions; the argument is the wavelength (interface variable emw.lambda or gop wavelength).

parameters.name: Piezoelectric: sE/cE, d/e, epsilon_rT/S
parameters.description: Given in strain-charge and stress-charge forms with the IEEE ordering; poling along the material z axis.

parameters.name: Nonlinear magnetic: B-H curve / H-B curve, J-A parameters
parameters.description: Interpolation functions used by Ampere's Law > B-H curve.

parameters.name: Semiconductor: band gap, affinity, effective DOS, mobilities, lifetimes
parameters.description: Used by the Semiconductor Material Model node.

tools.example:
rem Wave Optics: Add Material > Optical > Inorganic Materials > SiO2 (Malitson) > Add to Component
rem Wave Equation, Electric > Electric displacement field model: Refractive index (from material)
rem Frequency sweep: n is evaluated at each wavelength via the material function
tools.notes: Each library ships with its module; check the reference of each entry (shown in the material's description) for the valid wavelength/temperature/field range. Piezoelectric orientation is set through a Rotated System selected in the Piezoelectric Material node.

tools.name: .nas / .bdf / .inp / .msh mesh import formats
tools.description: Mesh files that Mesh > Import (and Geometry > Import for mesh-based geometry) reads: NASTRAN bulk data (.nas, .bdf, .nastran, .dat) with nodes and elements (tetra, hexa, prism, pyramid, tria, quad, first and second order) and optional PSHELL/PSOLID property IDs mapped to domains/boundaries, Abaqus (.inp, 6.x), VTK (.vtu/.vtk), PLY/STL/3MF surface meshes, COMSOL native .mphbin/.mphtxt, and the sectionwise/spreadsheet mesh text; imported meshes create geometry entities (domains/boundaries) by element groups so materials and physics can be assigned, and can be exported back with Results > Export > Mesh or Mesh > Export.
tools.usage: Mesh > Import (imp1) > Source: Mesh file > Filename: part.nas > Import; options: Boundary partitioning (automatic by angle / from file groups), Element type conversion; API: model.component("comp1").mesh("mesh1").create("imp1", "Import"); imp1.set("source", "nastran"); imp1.set("filename", "C:/mesh/part.nas"); mesh1.run()

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: nastran | vtk | stl | ply | 3mf | native (mphbin/mphtxt) | sectionwise | ...

parameters.name: Boundary partitioning
parameters.description: Split the surface into boundaries automatically (angle threshold) or by property IDs.

parameters.name: Domain/boundary from IDs
parameters.description: Create domains from element sets (PSOLID) and boundaries from shell elements (PSHELL).

parameters.name: Unit / scaling
parameters.description: Length unit of the file.

tools.notes: Imported meshes cannot be remeshed with COMSOL's mesher unless converted (Mesh > Import > Create geometry from mesh, or Geometry > Import of the mesh file with the 'Form solids from surface' option for STL). The 'Import (mesh)' entry in the Mesh chunk describes the node.

tools.name: .stl / .ply / .3mf surface mesh formats
tools.description: Triangulated surface formats: STL (binary/ASCII), PLY and 3MF are read by Geometry > Import (creating solid or surface geometry with faces partitioned by angle, optionally repaired and simplified with Remove Details) and by Mesh > Import (as boundary meshes), and written by Results > Export > Mesh/STL (e.g. a topology-optimised shape from a Filter dataset, a deformed configuration, or an isosurface) and by mphwritestl in MATLAB. Typical uses: scanned/medical geometry (with the mesh-to-geometry workflow), 3D printing of optimised designs, and exchange with visualisation tools.
tools.usage: Geometry > Import > Source: Mesh or 3D printing file (.stl/.ply/.3mf) > options: Form solids from surface objects, Partition faces by angle, Simplify mesh; Results > Export > Mesh > STL; API: geom Import feature set("type", "mesh"), set("filename", "scan.stl"), set("stlfacepartition", "auto")

parameters.name: Face partitioning
parameters.description: Automatic (by feature angle), manual angle, none, or from STL solids/PLY groups.

parameters.name: Simplify mesh / relative tolerance
parameters.description: Coarsen the triangulation before creating geometry faces.

parameters.name: Form solids
parameters.description: Close surfaces into solid objects.

parameters.name: Export: dataset, binary/ASCII
parameters.description: Which plot/dataset surface to write.

tools.notes: STL geometry has faceted faces; smoothing is not possible but Remove Details and the mesh simplification reduce element counts. For Boolean operations with CAD objects, convert with the geometry kernel after import (may fail for poor-quality scans).

tools.name: .vtu / .vtk (VTK) export and import
tools.description: VTK unstructured grid formats: Results > Export > Data with format 'VTK' (.vtu) writes expressions on the mesh (points, cells, point data per expression and per solution) for ParaView/VisIt postprocessing of large results or for coupling to other codes, and Mesh > Import reads VTK meshes (with cell data becoming element groups). Data export also offers 'Sectionwise' and 'Spreadsheet' text as alternatives.
tools.usage: Results > Export > Data (data1) > Expressions: T, spf.U > Output: File: result.vtu, Data format: VTK (or Sectionwise/Spreadsheet) > Export; API: model.result().export().create("data1", "Data"); data1.set("expr", new String[]{"T"}); data1.set("filename", "C:/out/T.vtu"); data1.set("struct", "vtk") (Data format list: spreadsheet | sectionwise | vtk); data1.run()

parameters.name: expr / unit
parameters.description: Expressions exported as point data.

parameters.name: struct
parameters.description: Data format: spreadsheet | sectionwise | vtk.

parameters.name: Points to evaluate in
parameters.description: Mesh nodes (element-based, keeps connectivity - needed for VTK) or a regular grid/custom points.

parameters.name: Solutions
parameters.description: All or selected times/parameters (VTK writes one array per solution or one file per step).

tools.notes: VTK export is available since 5.6 (cell/point data on the finite-element mesh, second-order elements are split). The 'Data (Export)' entry in the first Results chunk covers the text formats.

tools.name: Sectionwise and spreadsheet text data formats (.txt / .csv / .dat)
tools.description: COMSOL's two text layouts for tabulated data: Spreadsheet format has one header line (% x y z T) and one row per point with columns for coordinates (or function arguments) and values - the default for Export > Data on points/grids, for Interpolation function files, tables and probe exports; Sectionwise format lists coordinates, then elements (connectivity), then data sections (%Coordinates, %Elements, %Data with one column per expression/solution), preserving mesh connectivity so that exported results can be re-imported as an Interpolation function with exact element interpolation (e.g. transferring a field between models). Both accept comment lines starting with % and are readable by MATLAB/Python.
tools.usage: Results > Export > Data > Data format: Spreadsheet | Sectionwise; Global Definitions > Interpolation > Data source: File > Data format: Spreadsheet | Sectionwise (with 'Number of arguments' and 'Function name' per column); MATLAB: mphinterpolationfile writes spreadsheet files

parameters.name: Header line
parameters.description: % followed by column names (spreadsheet); section markers %Coordinates/%Elements/%Data (sectionwise).

parameters.name: Columns
parameters.description: Arguments/coordinates first, then one column per function/expression (and per solution for exports).

parameters.name: Separator
parameters.description: Spaces, tabs or commas (CSV) are accepted.

tools.example:
% spreadsheet file for a 2-argument interpolation function (x, y -> T)
% x y T
0 0 300
0.1 0 310
0 0.1 305
0.1 0.1 320

// COMSOL: Interpolation int1, Data source File, Data format Spreadsheet, Number of arguments 2, function name T
tools.notes: For large regular data use the 'Grid' format option of the Interpolation function (x, y, z grid vectors followed by the data block) which is far faster than scattered points.

tools.name: Touchstone (.s2p / .snp) S-parameter export
tools.description: RF Module export node that writes the S-parameter matrix of a multi-port model (from a Frequency Domain or Frequency Domain Source Sweep study) to a Touchstone file (.s1p, .s2p ... .snp) with selectable data format (magnitude/phase in dB or linear, real/imaginary), frequency unit and reference impedance, for use in circuit simulators (ADS, AWR, Keysight, LTspice) and measurement comparison. Touchstone files can also be imported by the Electrical Circuit interface as an S-parameter block (6.x) and by the RF Module's Lumped Element / port definitions.
tools.usage: Results > Export > Touchstone (tou1) > Filename: filter.s2p > Format: dB/angle | magnitude/angle | real/imag > Reference impedance > Export; API: model.result().export().create("tou1", "Touchstone"); tou1.set("filename", "C:/out/filter.s2p"); tou1.run()

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Output file; the extension sNp follows the number of ports.

parameters.name: Data format / frequency unit
parameters.description: DB | MA | RI; Hz/kHz/MHz/GHz.

parameters.name: Reference impedance
parameters.description: Port reference impedance written in the header (50 ohm default).

parameters.name: Ports / solutions
parameters.description: Port order and the solutions (frequencies) exported.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module. The S-parameter matrix must be complete (all ports excited) - use a Frequency Domain Source Sweep or a Port Sweep for multi-port devices.

tools.name: Image and animation output formats (PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF/EPS, GIF/AVI/WebM/MP4, image sequence)
tools.description: Graphics outputs of Results > Export: Image nodes write PNG (default, lossless), JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF and EPS/vector (for 1D plots) at a chosen pixel size, resolution (dpi) and antialiasing, with options for transparent background (PNG), legends, axes, title and logo; Animation nodes write animated GIF, AVI (Windows), WebM (6.x), MP4 (6.3, H.264) files or an image sequence (numbered PNG/JPEG frames) over time steps/parameters/eigenmodes or a rotating view, with frame count, frame rate, looping and size; the same settings apply to the in-GUI Player and to the Graphics window's Export toolbar button. Screenshots at print quality are best produced by the Image node with an explicit width in pixels and dpi.
tools.usage: Results > Export > Image > Format: PNG | JPEG | BMP | TIFF | GIF | EPS, Size: current | manual (width, height) | resolution (dpi); Results > Export > Animation > Output: File, Format: GIF | AVI | WebM | MP4 | Image sequence, Frames: Number of frames / Frame rate; API: export("img1").set("imagetype", "png"); export("anim1").set("type", "movie"); set("movietype", "gif"|"avi"|"webm"|"mp4"); set("framesel", "all"|"number"); set("frames", 60)

parameters.name: imagetype / pngfilename / jpgfilename ...
parameters.description: Image format and filename properties of the Image node.

parameters.name: width / height / resolution / antialias / background
parameters.description: Size and rendering options.

parameters.name: movietype / fps / frames / repeat
parameters.description: Animation container, frame rate, number of frames and looping.

parameters.name: Sequence type
parameters.description: Stored solutions | Dynamic data extension (interpolated frames) | Rotation (view rotation) | Parameter sweep.

tools.notes: Batch generation of images/animations needs a graphics-capable process (comsol batch -graphics or the Desktop). The 'Animation' entry in the first Results chunk introduces the node.

tools.name: .dxf / .step / .iges / .x_t / .sat CAD interchange formats (summary)
tools.description: Geometry file formats by licence: the core product imports 2D DXF (AutoCAD drawings as curves/solids) and COMSOL native .mphbin/.mphtxt and exports .mphbin/.mphtxt and DXF; the CAD Import Module, Design Module and LiveLink for CAD products add STEP (.step/.stp, AP203/AP214), IGES (.igs/.iges), Parasolid (.x_t/.x_b, native kernel format - most reliable), ACIS (.sat/.sab), and native SOLIDWORKS/Inventor/Creo/NX/Solid Edge/CATIA V5 (with File Import for CATIA V5) parts and assemblies for import, and Parasolid/ACIS/STEP/IGES for export; the ECAD Import Module reads ODB++, IPC-2581, GDS-II and NETEX-G for PCB and MEMS layouts as extruded layer stacks. Units, assembly structure (as separate objects) and selections/colours from CAD are preserved where the format carries them.
tools.usage: Geometry > Import > Source: CAD file / ECAD file / DXF file (extension selects the reader); Geometry > Export > Parasolid/ACIS/STEP/IGES/DXF/COMSOL; ECAD: Geometry > Import > ECAD with layer selection and height settings

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: step | iges | x_t/x_b | sat/sab | dxf | native CAD | ecad (odb++, ipc2581, gds, netex-g).

parameters.name: Length unit / import tolerance
parameters.description: From file or overridden; repair tolerance.

parameters.name: ECAD layer options
parameters.description: Which layers, thicknesses, dielectric layers, and whether to import as 2D or extruded 3D.

parameters.name: Export options
parameters.description: Objects to export, kernel format, version.

tools.notes: See the 'CAD Import' and 'Export (geometry)' entries in the geometry chunk for feature details; STEP/IGES imports may need Repair/Remove Details, Parasolid seldom does. Meshes (.nas, .stl) are a separate route through Mesh > Import.

tools.name: .mphphb / .mphapp / .mphbin and other COMSOL file types (summary)
tools.description: COMSOL-specific file types beyond .mph: .mphapp (applications saved for COMSOL Server / Compiler - a .mph with the Application Builder content and the application flag; plain .mph files also carry apps), .mphphb (Physics Builder files and compiled physics archives), .mphbin/.mphtxt (binary/text geometry and mesh interchange), .java/.class/.m/.vba (model files in programming languages), .lic licence files (FlexNet), the recovery directories and .status files written by batch runs, and the user preferences folder (.comsol/v63 under the user's home) holding preference files, GUI configuration, downloaded Application Library models and the Model Manager local database. Report templates and result templates are stored inside the preferences and the .mph itself rather than as separate files. Knowing these helps when sharing models: ship the .mph plus any external data files referenced by Interpolation/Import nodes unless they were embedded with Import Data.
tools.usage: File > Save As: COMSOL Multiphysics Model (.mph), Application (.mphapp), Model File for Java (.java), Model File for MATLAB (.m), Model File for VBA (.vba); Geometry/Mesh > Export: .mphbin/.mphtxt; Physics Builder: .mphphb; batch: .status, recovery directory; preferences: %USERPROFILE%/.comsol/v63

parameters.name: .mph / .mphapp
parameters.description: Model and application containers (zip-like binary).

parameters.name: .mphphb
parameters.description: Physics Builder file / archive.

parameters.name: .mphbin / .mphtxt
parameters.description: Native geometry and mesh interchange.

parameters.name: .java / .class / .m / .vba
parameters.description: Model files as source code.

parameters.name: .status / recovery
parameters.description: Batch progress and recovery data.

parameters.name: Embedded data
parameters.description: Import Data / 'Store in model' options embed CAD, mesh and table files inside the .mph.

tools.example:
rem make a model self-contained before sharing:
rem Interpolation > Import Data; Geometry > Import > Import Data; Materials with functions are already embedded
rem then File > Compact History and Save
tools.notes: Models saved by newer versions cannot be opened by older ones (no backward compatibility); .java/.m model files are the version-robust alternative when the API did not change. The meta.json of this catalog lists the main formats with descriptions.
